led-zeppelin.about: Recorded at Olympic Studios in London in October 1968, mostly played live in the room, and paid for by Jimmy Page and Peter Grant before the band had a record deal. Atlantic signed them on the strength of the tapes. Blues standards sit beside folk and the band's own heavy originals.
led-zeppelin.cover: Sam Shere's photograph of the Hindenburg airship burning at Lakehurst, New Jersey, in 1937, redrawn as a line image by George Hardie. The earliest UK copies printed the band name and the Atlantic logo in turquoise; they were soon switched to orange, and the turquoise sleeve is now a collector's item.
influence: Richard Linklater named his 1993 film Dazed and Confused after the song.
Dazed and Confused and Communication Breakdown stayed in the live set for years; Dazed was still there at the O2 reunion in 2007.

led-zeppelin-ii.about: Written and recorded on the move during 1969, in studios in London, New York, Los Angeles and Vancouver between tour dates, then mixed by Page with engineer Eddie Kramer in New York. In December 1969 it replaced the Beatles' Abbey Road at the top of the US chart.
led-zeppelin-ii.cover: Based on a photograph of a German First World War fighter squadron, with the faces of the band and others pasted in. Designed by David Juniper.
influence: An instrumental version of Whole Lotta Love by CCS was the theme tune of BBC television's Top of the Pops through the 1970s.
Moby Dick became the frame for John Bonham's drum solo on stage, which could run for well over a quarter of an hour.

led-zeppelin-iii.about: Much of it was written in 1970 at Bron-Yr-Aur, a cottage in mid Wales with no electricity, after the band's first long run of tours. The second side is almost all acoustic, which surprised some listeners at the time.
led-zeppelin-iii.cover: Designed by Zacron. A card wheel sits inside the gatefold sleeve; turning it shows different pictures through holes cut in the front.
influence: Immigrant Song was used in School of Rock (2003) after Jack Black filmed a plea to the band for permission, and again in Thor: Ragnarok (2017).

led-zeppelin-iv.about: Recorded mainly at Headley Grange, an old house in Hampshire, with the Rolling Stones' mobile studio parked outside, so the band could set up wherever the sound was best. John Bonham's drums for When the Levee Breaks were recorded in the stairwell. It was released with no title and no band name on the sleeve.
led-zeppelin-iv.cover: A 19th-century painting of an old man carrying sticks, which Robert Plant bought in a junk shop in Reading, hung on the wall of a half-demolished house. Inside is The Hermit, a tarot-style drawing by Barrington Colby. The inner sleeve carries the four members' symbols and a fifth for guest singer Sandy Denny.
influence: The guitar-shop scene in Wayne's World (1992) turns on a sign banning Stairway to Heaven.
Bonham's opening beat on When the Levee Breaks became one of the most sampled drum breaks in hip hop, starting with the Beastie Boys in 1986.
Certified 24 times platinum in the United States.

houses-of-the-holy.about: Recorded through 1972, partly with the Rolling Stones' mobile studio at Stargroves, Mick Jagger's country house. More keyboards and a wider range than before: reggae on D'yer Mak'er, funk on The Crunge, and the long, quiet Rain Song. The first Led Zeppelin album with a title.
houses-of-the-holy.cover: A Hipgnosis design: photographs of two children climbing the basalt columns of the Giant's Causeway in County Antrim, Northern Ireland, repeated and tinted orange and purple.
influence: The title song was left off and turned up two years later on Physical Graffiti.
No Quarter became one of the long showpieces of the 1973 to 1977 shows, built around John Paul Jones at the keyboards.

physical-graffiti.about: A double album. Eight songs were recorded at Headley Grange in early 1974; seven held back from the III, IV and Houses of the Holy sessions make up the rest. The first Led Zeppelin release on the band's own label, Swan Song.
physical-graffiti.cover: A photograph of two tenement buildings on St Mark's Place in New York's East Village, with the windows cut out. Different inner sleeves show through them, so what you see in each window changes. Designed by Peter Corriston and nominated for a Grammy for best album package.
influence: The same front steps appear in the Rolling Stones' 1981 video for Waiting on a Friend.

presence.about: Made in about three weeks at Musicland Studios in Munich at the end of 1975, while Robert Plant was recovering from a car crash on Rhodes and sang from a wheelchair. Guitar-led throughout, with no keyboards and no acoustic songs.
presence.cover: A Hipgnosis series of 1950s-style photographs, each featuring a small black obelisk the designers called the Object.

in-through-the-out-door.about: Recorded in late 1978 at Polar Studios in Stockholm, the studio ABBA had just built. John Paul Jones and Robert Plant wrote more of it than usual, and Jones's keyboards shape the sound. It was the last album released while John Bonham was alive.
in-through-the-out-door.cover: Issued in six different sleeves, each showing the same bar scene from a different person's point of view, packed in a plain brown paper bag so buyers could not tell which one they had. Brushing the inner sleeve with water brought out colour.

coda.about: Eight recordings from 1970 to 1978 that had not been released, put out two years after the band split. It includes a Bonham drum piece recorded in Montreux and three songs from the In Through the Out Door sessions.

the-song-remains-the-same.about: The soundtrack to the concert film, recorded over three nights at Madison Square Garden in New York in July 1973. Both film and album came out in 1976, while the band were off the road after Plant's accident.
